name: Gravity canals, upper Zaña valley, northern Peru
summary: Narrow, partly stone-lined gravity canals led stream water to terrace plots in the Ñanchoc valley of northern Peru, the earliest irrigation canals known in South America.
description: Preceramic people in the upper Zaña valley dug narrow gravity canals from the Ñanchoc stream along the contour to plots on a low terrace, three of them superimposed over time. The lowest confirmed canal dates to about 5,400 radiocarbon years BP, calibrated to about 4360-3990 BCE, and the authors infer communal labour to build and maintain the canals within an economy that still included hunting and gathering.

impact.note: The evidence is a few short canals in one small valley, reused there over several thousand years, and descent of later coastal Andean irrigation from them is not shown, so reach is held at regional and generativity at none; watering plots in a dry valley was a new capability within a still mixed farming and foraging economy.

date.label: c. 4360-3990 BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The lowest of three superimposed canals in the Ñanchoc valley, Canal 3, is dated to 6,310-5,940 cal. years BP, taken as about 4360-3990 BCE.

evidence.supports: Canal 3 dates to 5,380 ± 80 14 C yr B.P. (6,310-5,940 cal. yr B.P., Beta-154127)
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Evidence for the three directly superimposed canals'

date.label: c. 3100-2910 BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Canal 2, a higher superimposed canal, is dated to 5,050-4,860 cal. years BP, taken as about 3100-2910 BCE.

evidence.supports: It dates to 4,390 ± 40 14 C yr B.P. (5,050-4,860 cal. yr B.P., Beta-182966)
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Evidence for the three directly superimposed canals'

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: A possible fourth canal below Canal 3 is dated 6,705 ± 75 radiocarbon years BP (8,040-7,340 cal. BP); the paper treats it as possible only.
Whether the valley-wide and inter-valley canal systems of the Moche and Chimú descend from these canals is not covered by the source read.
The lead's 'possibly c. 4700 BCE' was not found in the paper.

research.note: Dillehay and colleagues call the Zaña valley canals the earliest known in South America, and contact with Old World irrigators at this date was impossible.
